# A Codex seat on Windows runs shell commands in its sandbox, and the probe proves it
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #297, sha256:d05080d4696ce2c94dc9b639ad7ee274909ce3ffcf326b8c34745040955a368d). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Draft
- **Shape:** Contract
- **Type:** bug
- **Repository:** mob-defaults (mob-crosscli: the driver probe and seat placement; the default templates' setup notes)
- **Source:** card 230 green 1 attempt 1 (2026-11-04 18:39 UTC). Codex CLI 0.149.1 with `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"` in ~/.codex/config.toml launches its shell as `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe`, a Microsoft Store app-execution alias to `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.PowerShell_7.6.9.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe\pwsh.exe`. The sandboxed process cannot open it: `CreateProcessAsUserW failed: 1920 (The file cannot be accessed by the system.)`. Reproduced in a fresh empty folder with `codex exec "Run the shell command: echo hello ..." -m gpt-5.6-sol -s workspace-write --skip-git-repo-check` (timed out after the error) and with `-s read-only` (replied with the same error instead of hello). Commands Codex routes through `C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe` succeed, so read-only seats that fall back to cmd still work, and voting needs no shell. No PowerShell is installed outside the Store package. The driver probe asks only for the word OK, so it reports Codex available while its sandboxed shell cannot start. The same class of defect as Muse's sandbox before its one-time setup.
- **Depends on:** none
- **Actor:** the driver probe and the seat placement for a Codex seat that runs commands
- **Given:** a Windows machine where Codex's sandboxed shell cannot start (for example pwsh only as a Store app alias)
- **Observes:** the probe runs one shell command under the sandbox mode the seat will use and records its output; a Codex build seat is placed only when that passes, and the setup notes name the one-time fix (a non-Store PowerShell, or Codex configured to use cmd)
- **Fails with:** a probe failure that names the shell path, the sandbox mode and the Windows error, instead of a seat that starts and cannot run a command
- **Invariants:** Codex voting and read-only seats keep working; no sandbox is bypassed to make the probe pass
- **Enables:** card 216 (the default templates carry backends that work for every enabled driver; here, Codex back in build seats on Windows)
- **One observable behaviour:** a Codex seat that is placed to run commands can run them, and one that cannot is refused before it starts, with the reason.
- **Done checks (at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. With the shell blocked as above, the probe for a command-running Codex seat fails and names the shell path, the sandbox mode and error 1920. ZOMBIES to be written by QA at ready.
  2. With the one-time fix applied, the same probe passes and a Codex green seat runs a command and commits on main in the one checkout under the single-writer lock. ZOMBIES to be written by QA at ready.
  3. A voting or read-only Codex seat is still placed when only the command probe fails. ZOMBIES to be written by QA at ready.

## Context

- Filed by the facilitator on 2026-11-04 from card 230 green 1 attempt 1; reproduced the same day (scratchpad codex-ws-repro, recorded in .mob/records/230/record-in-progress.json). A seat-placement defect, kept as a bug (D183). Applying the one-time fix on this machine (installing a non-Store PowerShell, or changing Codex's shell setting) is a machine change for the product owner to approve.
